methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective pilot study with small sample (n=17) and limited statistical power; acknowledged in manuscript. ROC analyses explicitly termed exploratory; AUC estimates have wide overlapping confidence intervals. Single experienced urologist scored nephrometry systems without inter-rater reliability assessment. Given limited cohort size and outcome events, formal statistical comparison of ROC curves was not performed, appropriately limiting claims to hypothesis-generating findings.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Prospective pilot study without control arm; feasibility-focused design. HA3D-based nephrometry offers potential clinical utility for surgical planning, but findings are preliminary and exploratory. Applicability depends on cost-effectiveness and workflow integration, neither of which is established. Represents early evidence in development of a potentially clinically relevant tool.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods section is transparent with clear description of nephrometry scoring, 3D model generation, surgical techniques, and outcome definitions. However, manuscript lacks pre-registration statement, protocol publication reference, and explicit data availability statement. Clavien-Dindo classification appropriately used for complications, but reproducibility limited by single-center design and single rater for nephrometry.

novelty_literature.justification: Directly compares 3D-based versus conventional 2D CT-derived nephrometry scores prospectively, extending prior cross-sectional observations. While prior studies demonstrated 3D models lead to complexity downgrading, this pilot compares predictive performance for perioperative outcomes and renal function using ROC analysis, representing an incremental methodological advancement in a growing application area.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear introduction explaining precision surgery context, comprehensive methods, transparent limitations section explicitly noting small sample size as limiting factor, and appropriate use of figures and heat maps. Discussion appropriately interprets findings as exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than definitive. Minor improvements possible in condensing supplementary data presentation.

key_strengths: Prospective within-patient comparison design eliminates anatomical heterogeneity as confound; direct comparison of 2D versus 3D scores from identical imaging dataset
Comprehensive outcome assessment including operative time, complications (Clavien-Dindo), and early renal function at multiple timepoints
Transparent acknowledgment of limitations; authors appropriately frame results as hypothesis-generating and exploratory rather than definitive
Focused cohort selection (intermediate to high-complexity tumors) represents clinically relevant population where anatomical assessment is most challenging
key_concerns: Small pilot sample size (n=17) with limited outcome events severely restricts statistical power and stability of ROC curve estimates; wide overlapping confidence intervals prevent definitive conclusions
Single rater performed nephrometry scoring; inter-observer variability and inter-rater concordance not assessed despite reproducibility being critical for clinical adoption
Lack of formal statistical comparison between 2D and 3D ROC curves; DeLong test for complications but not performed for CKD endpoint due to limited events
Single-center design with three surgeons reduces generalizability; no assessment of learning curve or surgeon-specific variability
No cost-effectiveness analysis or workflow burden assessment despite these being acknowledged barriers to clinical adoption; feasibility of 3D modeling integration not addressed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Pilot feasibility study with appropriate exploratory design but insufficient sample size and statistical power to support clinical implementation claims. Suitable for Tier 4 journals publishing early-phase feasibility work; major revisions should address inter-rater reliability and cost-effectiveness considerations.
